tasks.constants: Use g = 9.80 m/s², +x right and +y up. Neglect air resistance unless stated otherwise.

questions.prompt: A ball launches at 18.0 m/s at 45.0° and lands at launch height. Find time to apex, total flight time, maximum height and range.

marking.point: Maximum height = uᵧ²/(2g) = 8.27 m above launch.

questions.prompt: A launcher has fixed speed 12.0 m/s. Can it reach a target 16.0 m away at launch height? Justify without guessing angles.

marking.point: Equal-height range is R = u² sin2θ/g.
Its maximum occurs at sin2θ = 1, θ = 45°.
The required 16.0 m exceeds this maximum, so no launch angle reaches the target under the model.

mastery.prompt: For equal launch and landing heights, total flight time is…
mastery.why: The rise and return take equal times; uᵧ/g is time to apex.

mastery.prompt: At equal-height landing, the speed without drag is…
mastery.why: Gravitational potential energy is unchanged between the endpoints.

mastery.prompt: Complementary launch angles share…
options: range at equal heights and fixed speed
mastery.why: The range contains sin2θ; time and height depend on the vertical component.

mastery.prompt: 45° maximises range for…
options: equal heights, fixed speed, constant g and no drag
mastery.why: The maximum follows from sin2θ = 1 under the stated assumptions.

questions.prompt: A ball launches at 12.0 m/s at 30.0° above horizontal from a 6.00 m platform. Find time to ground, range and impact speed.

marking.point: Select future root t = 1.88 s; discard the negative root.
Impact speed from v² = u² + 2gH is √261.6 = 16.2 m/s.

questions.prompt: A projectile has uₓ = 9.00 m/s and uᵧ = 12.0 m/s. Find both times it reaches 3.00 m above launch and the corresponding x-positions. Explain why height alone does not identify a target hit.

marking.point: Quadratic roots t = 0.283 s and 2.17 s.
The smaller root is rising; the larger root is falling, as vᵧ = 12.0 − 9.80t changes sign.
A target must match both x and y at the same time.

mastery.prompt: Landing 10 m below launch has Δy, with up positive,…
mastery.why: Δy is final minus initial height.

mastery.prompt: Two positive roots for an upward launch reaching a higher height describe…
mastery.why: The same reachable height can be crossed twice.

mastery.prompt: A negative discriminant means…
mastery.why: There is no real time satisfying the height condition.

mastery.prompt: At a lower landing the speed is…
options: greater than launch speed in the no-drag model

tasks.constants: Use g = 9.80 m/s². Structures are rigid and stationary; state support assumptions. Anticlockwise torque is positive.

questions.prompt: A uniform 5.00 m beam weighs 160 N and rests on end supports A and B. A 250 N point load acts 4.00 m from A. Find both support reactions.

marking.point: Beam weight acts 2.50 m from A.
Vertical balance: Rₐ + 280 = 410 gives Rₐ = 130 N upward.

questions.prompt: A uniform 6.00 m beam weighing 200 N rests on unbolted supports at x = 0 and x = 4.00 m. A 600 N person walks onto the overhang. Find the position x where tipping begins.

marking.point: At impending tipping the x = 0 support reaction is zero.
Take moments about the support at x = 4.00 m.
x = 4.00 + 200/600 = 4.33 m from the left end.
Further motion would require a downward reaction at the unbolted left support, so two-contact equilibrium fails.

mastery.prompt: Taking moments about A removes Rₐ because…
mastery.why: Its line of action passes through the pivot.

mastery.prompt: A uniform beam weight acts at…
mastery.why: Uniform mass distribution puts its centre of mass halfway along.

mastery.prompt: Two supports share a load equally when…
options: the complete load and geometry are symmetric
mastery.why: Force balance alone gives the total, while symmetry and moment balance give equal sharing.

mastery.prompt: A fixed cantilever support must usually supply…
options: a force and a reaction moment
mastery.why: The clamp balances both net force and net torque.

tasks.constants: Extension beyond the assessed 2026 velocity-transformation equations. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s. One-dimensional inertial frames; +x to the right.

questions.prompt: Extension: A travels at +0.80c and B at −0.30c in Earth frame, with A initially left of B. Find A’s signed velocity measured by B and distinguish it from Earth’s closing rate.

marking.point: The closing rate is a separation rate in Earth coordinates; it is not B’s measured object speed.

questions.prompt: Extension: A ship moves at +0.50c relative to Earth. A probe moves backwards at −0.80c relative to the ship. Find its Earth velocity and interpret its sign.

marking.point: Transform from ship to Earth: u = (u′ + v)/(1 + u′v/c²).
Unlike some backward ship-frame launches, this probe also moves backwards in Earth frame; the sign follows the calculation.

mastery.prompt: The inverse transformation expects u and v to be measured…
mastery.why: u is the object and v the observer velocity in S.

mastery.prompt: Two ships each at 0.60c approach in Earth frame. One measures the other’s speed as…
mastery.why: 1.20/1.36 = 0.882; 1.20c is the Earth-coordinate closing rate.

mastery.prompt: A negative u′ means…

questions.prompt: Calculate energy to turn 0.0500 kg ice at −20.0°C into water at 30.0°C. Use the stated thermal constants and neglect losses.

marking.point: Distinct state and phase-change terms are required; one mcΔT term is insufficient.

questions.prompt: 0.120 kg ice at 0°C absorbs 20 040 J. Calculate melted mass, remaining ice mass and final temperature.

marking.point: Energy to melt all ice = 0.120 × 334 000 = 40 080 J, greater than available.

mastery.prompt: During ideal melting at constant temperature, internal energy…
mastery.why: Latent energy changes microscopic arrangement and potential energy.

mastery.prompt: Specific latent heat units are…
mastery.why: It is phase-change energy per mass.

mastery.prompt: If energy is insufficient to melt all the ice at 0°C, final state is…
options: ice and water at 0°C in the ideal model
mastery.why: Calculate the melted amount using Q/L.

mastery.prompt: To heat ice below 0°C into warm liquid, use…
options: one water c over the whole interval
